app_records.description: Wire 3.2: Paykit's member of an app record, protocols.paykit, as a Paykit reader reads it. Each record is the shop app record of the Switch set's documents.json with its paykit member changed or removed (and, for public endpoints with expires_at null, expires_at null too), signed again with the shop's signing key; the signatures verify. The switch takes every one, since it checks only the form of protocols (Switch wire 3.2). accepted are records a Paykit reader takes, the first the shop's record as it is; reads is what the reader takes from each: the Payment Endpoint Identifiers of capabilities.endpoint_identifiers, and the public endpoints. A missing or null paykit member, capabilities, endpoint_identifiers or public_endpoints reads as empty, and unknown members are ignored. refused are records Paykit's readers refuse, though the switch takes them (switch_accepts): a capabilities or public_endpoints that isn't an object, an endpoint_identifiers that isn't an array of strings, a payload that isn't a string, public endpoints with expires_at null, and, last, four that break wire 1.4: an endpoint identifier in capabilities that isn't a Payment Endpoint Identifier (btc-lightning/bolt11), a public endpoint key that isn't one (..), the reserved key private, and an empty payload. protocols and expires_at are the record's as signed. reason is the wording at a Paykit reader: the prototype's, and paykit-lib's for the last four.

certificate_rejections.description: Wire 3.1: certificates whose permissions are well formed but aren't exactly the list Paykit's table derives from their scopes (paykit_permissions). Each is the wallet certificate of the Switch set's documents.json with scopes and permissions changed, signed by alice's identity key; the signatures verify. The switch takes them and enforces exactly that list (switch_accepts), while Paykit's verifiers, apps and payers, refuse them. The lists that aren't well formed, which every verifier refuses, are the Switch set's permission_rejections. reason is the prototype's wording at a Paykit verifier.

certificates.description: Wire 3.1, Switch wire 3.1: the certificate of each app of keys.json, as Paykit's verifiers take it, in its carrying form (signed: body and sig). Each holds its app's keys, scopes and permissions as keys.json gives them, issued_at 2025-12-01T00:00:00.000Z and the app's expires_at, signed by its identity's key under pubky-switch/v1/app-cert. The executor's and the phone's are Paykit's own, the accepted certificates of executor_certificates and payer_certificates, holding contacts; the others are the certificates every other case of this set signs again with scopes or permissions changed. app is the app's name in keys.json.

description: Paykit's signed documents and Paykit's checks of the Switch's certificates and app records (wire 3): the executor grant, alone and as the Allowance record's grant history holds it, with Paykit's own executor certificate, and the Switch set's, which Paykit's verifiers refuse; Paykit's own phone certificate, and certificates holding pay without contacts, which they refuse; certificates that Paykit's verifiers refuse for their scopes or their permissions, certificates that hold another protocol's scopes beside Paykit's or instead of them, and app records as a Paykit reader reads their Paykit member. The certificates are the Switch set's documents.json certificates with scopes or permissions changed, and the app records its shop app record with its Paykit member changed.

executor_certificates.description: Spec 3.1, wire 3.1 and 3.3: the executor's certificate. allowance_execute requires allowance, pay and contacts, so that every executor reads the deny list. accepted is Paykit's own executor certificate, which the executor grant of this file carries: the Switch set's documents.json executor certificate with contacts added to its scopes and the permissions its scopes need, signed again by alice's identity key. refused is the Switch set's executor certificate as it is, which holds allowance_execute without contacts: the switch takes it (switch_accepts), and Paykit's verifiers refuse it. reason is paykit-lib's wording at a Paykit verifier.

extension_app.description: Wire 3.1, 3.2, Switch wire 3.1, 3.2: bob's extension app cap. certificate is its certificate of certificates, holding request beside the extension scope ext:paykit-cap. app_record is its app record, signed by its signing key under pubky-switch/v1/app-record: it carries that certificate, accepts the kinds a payee app takes from payers and the extension kind paykit-cap.offer, and its Paykit member states its endpoint identifiers and no public endpoints; its label is bob cap, its updated_at its certificate's issued_at, and its expires_at null. The switch takes the record, and a Paykit reader reads its member.

labelled_scope_rejections.description: Wire 3.1, Switch wire 3.1: certificates every verifier refuses for their labelled selling scopes request:<label> (a label is 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit; at most 8 per certificate; never beside plain request, which covers every label). Each is the hosted certificate with scopes changed and permissions derived from them, signed by bob's identity key; reason is the prototype's wording. switch_accepts says whether the switch takes it: its generic scope rule refuses a label of 33 characters, one that isn't valid, an empty one and plain request beside request:shop1, while nine labels break only Paykit's bound of 8.

multi_protocol_certificates.description: Wire 3.1, spec 3.2, Switch wire 3.1 "Several protocols" and "Scope roots": certificates that hold another protocol's scopes beside Paykit's or instead of them, and one whose extension prefix holds no -, as Paykit's verifiers check them. Each is the shop certificate of the Switch set's documents.json (the last, the cap certificate) with scopes and permissions changed, signed again by bob's identity key; the switch takes every one (switch_accepts). A scope whose root, the part before any :, isn't one of Paykit's reserved roots (pay, request, allowance, allowance_execute, contacts, manage_contacts and ext) is another protocol's, such as chat. paykit_scopes are the scopes Paykit reads, and paykit_permissions the list they need. A Paykit verifier requires every permission of paykit_permissions, and, when the certificate holds no other protocol's scope, permissions exactly that list. accepted are certificates Paykit's verifiers take: request beside chat, with lists.read, which chat needs, and conversation.add, which request needs; and chat alone with lists.read, a valid certificate that holds no Paykit scope, whose Paykit messages recipients drop at check 8 (messages.json multi_protocol_senders). refused are certificates they refuse: request beside chat without conversation.add; request alone with lists.read beside conversation.add; and request beside ext:cap, an extension scope whose prefix holds no -. reason is paykit-lib's wording at a Paykit verifier, of the first check that refuses it.

payer_certificates.description: Spec 3.1, wire 3.1: a paying app's certificate. pay requires contacts, so that every paying app reads the deny list and pays no counterparty the user blocked. accepted is Paykit's own phone certificate, which the phone's messages stored in sealed.json carry: the Switch set's documents.json phone certificate with contacts added to its scopes and the permissions its scopes need, signed again by alice's identity key. refused are the Switch set's phone certificate as it is, which holds pay and allowance without contacts, and the Switch set's wallet certificate with pay alone and the permissions pay needs, signed again by alice's identity key: the switch takes each (switch_accepts), and Paykit's verifiers refuse each. reason is paykit-lib's wording at a Paykit verifier.
